clue.text: Falsifies triplet with note for one such

blocks.note: to fiddle accounts is to falsify them
a trin is an old word for one of three children born at a birth
a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Someone cooks the books in threes and adds a note to cover one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One such' points back to the fiddles at the start: the answer, FIDDLESTRING, is one of the strings of a fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the strings stretched along a violin is a fiddlestring, so it is one such item belonging to a fiddle.

clue.text: Theatre critic often, one struggling to take in half of Strindberg's concoction?

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up from ingredients, so the letters are jumbled
taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other
only the front half of the playwright's name is used, the rest discarded

blocks.note: someone who struggles or battles
the first five of the ten letters of the Swedish playwright's name

explanation.surface: A drama critic, perhaps a struggling one, tries to digest half a Strindberg play.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled half-name goes inside after the first two letters of the fighter. Critics traditionally attend opening nights, hence 'often'.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-nighter is a habitual attender of opening performances, which reviewers of plays usually are.

clue.text: What may be used to calculate oil flow in damaged side-car

definitions.text: What may be used to calculate oil flow

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the hyphenated word supplies its seven letters

explanation.surface: Oil is leaking from a wrecked motorcycle side-car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil flow' suggests the sidecar's leak, but it is the flow of oil through rock that petroleum engineers measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The darcy is a unit of permeability, used to work out how readily oil moves through porous rock.

clue.text: Old shilling, not nearly new, fetching high price

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to take the following letters out of the coin's name
nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: deaner was old slang for a shilling
the word for new with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: An old shilling, though far from new, sells for a high price to collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: Take NE out of DEANER to leave DEAR. A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin worth twelve pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dear is expensive, so it commands or fetches a high price.

clue.text: One game in Scotland in which there's very little between the two sides?

indicators.note: something lying between two others sits in the middle of them

blocks.note: left and right, the two sides
'a mite' means a very little, as in 'a mite tired'

explanation.surface: A Scottish game played so evenly that there is barely anything between the two teams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' here is the old adjective for a lame leg, not a sport: a lamiter is a cripple in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamiter is a Scottish word for a lame person, and game describes a crippled leg.

clue.text: E.g. sea bream special, very dry

blocks.note: SP is an abbreviation of special
arid land is extremely dry

explanation.surface: A dried-out sea bream offered as the special on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparids are the family of fishes to which the sea bream belongs, so the bream is an example.

clue.text: A prank

blocks.note: surface reading: a practical joke played on someone
setter's reading: just the definition, since this is the word solvers write their own clues for

explanation.walkthrough: This was the Azed competition word: the puzzle gives only a definition, and entrants submit their own clues for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical joke or hoax played on someone is a common synonym for this word.

clue.text: I produce something like cork and relock bottled end of jeroboam (7, two words)

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
bottled is slang for drunk, and drunken letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before mixing
a jeroboam is a large wine bottle

explanation.surface: A cork producer explains how to reseal a jeroboam of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled' looks like part of the wine picture, but it signals the mix; the surface 'cork' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock elm is an American elm whose twigs develop thick corky ridges of bark.

clue.text: Cubic mineral not brought in by the tide? On the contrary

indicators.note: being brought in by something means being taken inside it
this swaps the roles just described, so the outer and inner pieces trade places

blocks.note: non is the Latin for not, familiar as a prefix
the tide stands for the sea

explanation.surface: A cubic crystal that the tide has failed to wash up onto the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'not' would go inside 'tide'; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so the tide goes inside 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosean is a mineral of the sodalite group that crystallises in the cubic system.

clue.text: One's surely lying badly about 'tip of blue' in this scarlet flower (12, two words)

indicators.note: doing something badly gets it out of order, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the single one
the tip of a word is one of its ends, here the final letter

blocks.note: the two words supply eleven letters to mix
the colour word's final letter

explanation.surface: Anyone claiming this scarlet flower has a blue tip must be lying.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'tip of blue' is its last letter, not its first. The Guernsey lily is named after the Channel Island where it was naturalised.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guernsey lily, Nerine sarniensis, is a South African bulb bearing heads of brilliant red blooms.

clue.text: Naiad upset about 'second' for Hera, re judgement of Paris?

indicators.note: upsetting something throws it into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the mixed letters surround the chosen one
the second letter of the goddess's name is the one taken

blocks.note: a water nymph, taken as written
Hera is queen of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A water nymph is upset at coming second in the beauty contest Paris judged, Hera's position.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris judged Hera, Athena and Aphrodite on Mount Ida, so anything concerning that judgement relates to Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaean means of Mount Ida, the setting where the Trojan prince chose the fairest goddess.

clue.text: Best —— may be involved in turning breads out

definitions.text: Best —— may be involved in turning breads out

indicators.note: turning things over mixes them, so the letters are rearranged
the blank plus the first word make up the mix, so the first word's letters are taken away to leave the blank

blocks.note: the two words supply nine letters
taken as written, to be removed from the mix

explanation.surface: The finest grain of some kind may go into making breads.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the blank, filled with the answer and put beside 'Best', rearranges to 'breads out'. Read whole, the clue also says the grain goes into bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Doura, also spelt durra, is a sorghum grown as a cereal crop and ground for flour.

clue.text: Favouring very good food-grain

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
so, as an exclamation of approval, is a curt way of saying 'very good'

explanation.surface: Someone shows a preference for a cereal of excellent quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very good' reads as praise of the grain, but it is a single word of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Proso is a millet, Panicum miliaceum, grown as a cereal crop for flour and fodder.

clue.text: Running race is ideal? So open to non-professionals, dear

indicators.note: running things are in motion, so the letters move into a new order
the answer and the last word together make up the mixed phrase, so that word's letters are subtracted

blocks.note: three words supplying eleven letters
taken as written, to be removed from the mix

explanation.surface: Amateurs could take part if the running race were made open, the question suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus 'dear' together rearrange to 'race is ideal'. 'So open' asks for a verb meaning to open in that way.
explanation.definitionFit: To laicise is to hand something over to lay people rather than clergy or professionals.

clue.text: Mixed curries — one may have lumps in

indicators.note: mixed things are stirred together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, before mixing

explanation.surface: A dish of mixed curries, one of them lumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lumps' suggests a badly made sauce, but they are lumps of sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucrier is a sugar bowl, a container that holds sugar lumps.

clue.text: Cocktail with a bit of Enzian in vat

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter
the drink has the single letter with it, held inside, as the closing 'in' confirms

blocks.note: kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur
Enzian is a German gentian spirit

explanation.surface: A cocktail mixed in a vat with a dash of Enzian schnapps.
explanation.definitionFit: A kier is a large vat in which cloth is boiled for bleaching.

clue.text: Dreary old versifier? Not me

indicators.note: 'Not me' says that the two-letter pronoun is left out of the word

blocks.note: a metrist is a writer of verse, skilled in metre
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A gloomy poet of the past protests that the description does not fit him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the definition: trist is an archaic word, so the answer is a dreary word from old usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Trist is an obsolete form of triste, meaning sad or sorrowful.

clue.text: Label bed to be brought back for old foot soldier

indicators.note: bringing something back sends it the other way, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: a name is a label
kip is slang for a bed or sleep

explanation.surface: A tag on a bed that has to be returned, labelled for an old soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: NAME and KIP together are reversed as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: A pikeman was an infantryman armed with a long pike, a soldier of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Former skin spots? One among a number returning

indicators.note: being among something means sitting inside it
returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: any number will do; this one has the right letters
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Someone recalls old skin blemishes, one among several that keep coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into the number and the whole is then reversed. 'Former' marks the obsolete spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Naeve is an old form of naevus, a birthmark or mole on the skin.

clue.text: Cry of distress from tug I spotted crashing into vessel

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are rearranged
going into something puts it inside, so the mix sits in the vessel

blocks.note: vas is the anatomical term for a duct or vessel
the boat plus the letter I, which is spotted because it carries a dot

explanation.surface: A distress call goes up as a tug is seen ramming into a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks nautical, but it is the anatomical vas. 'Spotted' describes the dotted letter i.
explanation.definitionFit: Vagitus is the first cry of a newborn baby, a wail of distress at birth.

clue.text: Leaping catch — man out — I pocketed in covers

indicators.note: leaping letters jump out of their places, so they are rearranged
out can mean disordered, so these letters are rearranged too
something pocketed is tucked inside, so the single letter goes within

blocks.note: to get is to catch
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a leaping catch, the batsman out, and I took the ball in the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words mislead: 'covers' is the fielding position in the surface but the definition here, wing cases of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Tegmina are the hardened forewings of grasshoppers and beetles that protect the hind wings.

clue.text: For Jews it's symbolic, sticking flower in cap

indicators.note: something stuck in a thing is fixed inside it

blocks.note: a cap is a kind of hat
a flower

explanation.surface: Pinning a flower to a cap carries symbolic meaning in Jewish custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Haroset is the fruit and nut paste of the Passover meal, representing the mortar Hebrew slaves used in Egypt.

clue.text: Ligaments? One not far from foot when raised

indicators.note: raising a down entry lifts it upwards, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a means one
near is the opposite of far
F is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A doctor asks whether the ligaments in question lie near the foot when it is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads one, not far, foot; turned upwards it gives F, RAEN, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraena are small folds of membrane, such as the one under the tongue, that restrain an organ.

clue.text: Anzac swapping units (front and rear) given equipment

indicators.note: the single letters at the two ends change places

blocks.note: digger is the nickname for an Australian or New Zealand soldier

explanation.surface: An Anzac soldier swaps units and is issued with new kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Units' looks military but means single letters; an Anzac was a soldier of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigged means fitted out, as a ship is supplied with its sails and gear.

clue.text: Blowing kiss king's mistress turned in after a change of sheets?

indicators.note: to blow something is to lose it, so the kiss letter is lost from the royal word
something turned is facing the other way, so it is read backwards
in places the reversed piece inside what is left of the royal word

blocks.note: rex is the Latin for king
a cross at the end of a letter stands for a kiss
dame is an old word for the mistress of a household

explanation.surface: A king blows a kiss to his mistress, and they go to bed once the sheets are changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing kiss' looks like a romantic gesture, but it means dropping X from REX. 'Turned in' suggests going to bed; 'turned' and 'in' are two separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed with fresh linen put on it has been made up again, so it is newly made once more.

clue.text: Granular CO ? Cried after receiving treatment

indicators.note: treatment works something over, so the letters come out rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, before mixing

explanation.surface: Someone wept after medical treatment involving granular carbon dioxide.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' stands for the subscript 2 of CO2, lost from the clue text: the definition is granular carbon dioxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Drice is a name for dry ice in granulated form, solid carbon dioxide used as a coolant.

clue.text: Garb in grey no longer charms

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: gris is an obsolete word for grey
rig is an outfit of clothes

explanation.surface: Grey clothing has lost its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charms' reads as a verb in the surface but is a plural noun; 'no longer' marks the archaic word for grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigris are African amulets or talismans worn to ward off evil.

clue.text: Old-style verse he objectively included in school subject

indicators.note: something included in a thing is put inside it

blocks.note: RE is Religious Education, a British school subject
the objective case of he

explanation.surface: A teacher brings old-fashioned poetry he admires into a school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectively' is grammatical: it asks for the object form of the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhime is an old spelling of rhyme, meaning verse or poetry.

clue.text: Roller dispersing fellow's waste on board whaler?

indicators.note: dispersing something parts it, so the other piece goes into the gap

blocks.note: a guy is a fellow
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce, abbreviated RR

explanation.surface: A wave rolling across a whaling ship scatters a man's rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' suggests a wave, but it is British slang for a Rolls-Royce car.
explanation.definitionFit: Gurry is the offal and refuse left after cutting up a whale or fish.

clue.text: Pilgrim, one following god (not his) from the east

indicators.note: reading from the east in an across entry means going right to left
following puts the single letter second, after the god

blocks.note: Jah is the Rastafarian name for God
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pilgrim follows a god from the east, though not the god of his own faith.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not his)' is a surface aside: Jah is the Rastafarian deity, not the god of a Muslim pilgrim.
explanation.definitionFit: A haji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca.

clue.text: Okra merging with what it's fried in? It's painful in the mouth

indicators.note: merging makes two words share a letter where they meet, so one copy goes

blocks.note: gumbo is another name for okra
cooking fat used for frying

explanation.surface: Okra soaking up its frying oil makes a sore mouthful.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words overlap on their shared O.
explanation.definitionFit: A gumboil is an abscess on the gum, a painful swelling inside the mouth.

clue.text: What you'll see lags behind in short musical sections?

blocks.note: first meaning: lags are convicts, who are kept behind the metal rods of a cell
second meaning: the measures of a piece of music

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lags behind' reads as falling behind, but lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners are said to be behind them, and a score divides music into these short units of time.

clue.text: Typical satyr's behaviour, after wine I bet

blocks.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine
taken as written
a go is a turn or attempt, as in 'have a bet' on something

explanation.surface: A satyr behaves true to type after drinking, the speaker wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: Satyrs, the goat-legged followers of Bacchus, were proverbially lecherous.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentigo is morbid lustfulness, the defining trait of the mythical satyr.

clue.text: Long par with this pitch mark could make a lump on green

indicators.note: the words before could be rearranged to make the phrase that follows
the answer goes with the opening words in the mix, so their letters are taken off to leave it

blocks.note: four words supplying twelve letters
taken as written, to be removed from the mix

explanation.surface: A golfer's long par putt leaves a pitch mark that raises a lump on the green.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'long par' plus the answer rearranges to 'a lump on green'. 'Pitch' is musical here, not the golfer's pitch shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A neume is a sign in medieval plainsong notation showing the rise and fall in a melody.

clue.text: Pay out from urn excited Murray?

indicators.note: something excited is stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
the question mark admits a pun: Murray is said like moray, a kind of eel

explanation.surface: Cash is paid out of an urn to an excited Andy Murray, the tennis player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murray' looks like the tennis player, but the question mark lets it stand for the moray eel.
explanation.definitionFit: To unreel a line or rope is to let it run out, as one pays out a cable.

clue.text: No support for this quiche? Nasty party asides about recipe (12, two words)

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the words surround the single letter before mixing

blocks.note: two words supplying eleven letters
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Snide remarks at a party about a quiche recipe that no one supports.
explanation.walkthrough: A quiche bakes in a supporting dish, whereas this kind of crust stands up without one.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised pastry, as for a pork pie, is moulded to stand by itself, needing no tin to hold it up.
